newsitem.title: USA: Corporacion Andina de Fomento yankee subscribed 3x.
newsitem.headline: Corporacion Andina de Fomento yankee subscribed 3x.

text.p: Corporacion Andina de Fomento's (CAF) $150 million 10-year yankee issue was more than three times oversubscribed at a spread of 76 basis points over comparable T-notes, said Dan Vallimarescu, director of Merrill Lynch & Co Inc's capital markets group.
A second tranche of $50 million 20-year bonds priced at 91 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries. It was also oversubscribed, Villamarescu said.
He said the issue boasted perhaps the tigthest spread ever for a Latin American issuer, although he did not confirm the statistic.

CAF is a multilateral lending organization owned by shareholders in Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela. The organization is similar in scope to other multilaterals such as the Interamerican Development Bank, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank.
Villamarescu said the debt was sold to approximately 35 investors, many of whom are non-traditional buyers of Latin American securities.
"Now (CAF) is really perceived by investors as being part of that elite group of multi-laterals," he said."
He added CAF is rated significantly higher than its shareholding countries. The deal is rated Baa2 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB-plus by Standard & Poor's.
